construct: KISS1R is the kisspeptin receptor expressed on GnRH neurons. Kisspeptin activation of KISS1R depolarizes GnRH neurons and stimulates GnRH secretion; inactivating KISS1R variants can cause normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and failure of normal pubertal activation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Absent puberty with low sex steroid and low gonadotropins, normal smell, normal pituitary imaging, and biallelic KISS1R loss identifies normosmic isolated GnRH deficiency from failure of kisspeptin activation of GnRH neurons.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Pituitary GnRH-receptor signaling, Leydig-cell LH signaling, inhibin feedback, and androgen-receptor signaling are all downstream or different regulatory steps and are not KISS1R.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The normal smell and KISS1R genotype localize the defect to hypothalamic kisspeptin-GnRH activation rather than GnRH-neuron migration or pituitary/gonadal signaling.
